questions.question: Many employers now list creativity and problem solving among the top skills they want in new hires. Employers value these innovation skills mainly because
questions.explanation: Needs and technology keep changing. Innovation skills, such as creativity, curiosity, and problem solving, help businesses develop new products and better processes as customer needs and technology change. Products do need to change to stay competitive, innovation involves some risk, and competitors regularly introduce new products. Innovation doesn't only mean inventing new products; it can also mean finding better ways to serve customers or run operations. Employers often ask about innovation in interviews because they want people who can solve problems creatively.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the need for innovation skills

questions.question: A sales manager is scheduling a dinner with clients during a religious holiday that involves fasting for some of the clients. What is the most culturally sensitive action?

options.A: Schedule more dinners during the holiday
options.B: Keep the dinner and ignore the holiday
options.C: Ask about preferences and adjust the plans
options.D: Tell the clients to skip their fast

questions.explanation: Ask about preferences and adjust the plans. Asking clients about their preferences and adjusting plans, such as scheduling after the holiday or choosing a different meeting format, shows respect for their beliefs. Ignoring the holiday, adding more dinners, or asking them to break their fast would be insensitive and could harm the relationship. Many businesses keep a calendar of major cultural and religious holidays to help with scheduling. Asking respectfully shows the clients that the sales manager values them as people, not just as customers.

questions.question: Which type of insurance would a young adult who drives to work most need by law in most states?
questions.explanation: Auto liability insurance. Most states require drivers to carry auto liability insurance, which pays for damage or injuries the driver causes to others. Pet, travel, and wedding insurance are optional and cover specific situations. Determining insurance needs involves looking at legal requirements, risks, and what a person could afford to lose. Drivers may also choose collision and comprehensive coverage to protect their own vehicles. Determining insurance needs means looking at legal requirements, possible losses, and what a person can afford. People should review their coverage when their lives change, such as when they buy a home or have children.

questions.question: Marketing is important in a global economy because it
questions.explanation: Helps reach customers worldwide. Marketing helps businesses learn about customers in different countries and adapt products, prices, distribution, and promotion to meet their needs. This lets companies grow beyond their home markets. Marketing doesn't eliminate competition, governments and markets influence prices in each country, and marketing can't replace the need for good products. For example, a company might change a product's name, packaging, or advertising for different countries. Global marketing also helps businesses find new customers when growth slows at home.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain marketing and its importance in a global economy

questions.question: Sienna's sales goal for the month is 40 units. By the third week, she has already sold 38. Which response best shows an achievement orientation?

options.A: Stop working hard until next month
options.C: Set a higher target this month
options.D: Lower her goal for next month

questions.explanation: Set a higher target this month. People with an achievement orientation look for ways to exceed expectations and keep improving. Setting a new, higher target keeps Sienna challenged and motivated. Coasting for the rest of the month, discouraging coworkers, or lowering future goals shows a lack of drive. Setting stretch goals can also prepare her for advancement. Achievement-oriented people often celebrate progress but keep looking for the next challenge. Sienna might also share what is working so teammates can improve their own results.

questions.question: After research shows that 60% of a store's customers want to shop online, the most actionable recommendation would be to

options.D: conduct more research for another year.

questions.explanation: Open an online store. Actionable recommendations turn findings into clear, practical steps. Launching an online store for popular products responds directly to customer demand. More research may delay action without adding value, ignoring results wastes the research, and closing the physical store goes too far because 40% of customers may still prefer shopping in person. The store could start with its best-selling products to test demand before expanding, which limits risk. Good recommendations also include who will be responsible and when the action should happen.

performanceIndicator.text: Translate research findings into actionable business recommendations

questions.question: Which form of financial exchange immediately takes money from the buyer's bank account?
questions.explanation: Debit card. A debit card transaction withdraws money directly from the buyer's checking account, usually within moments. A credit card lets the buyer borrow money and pay later, layaway reserves an item until it is paid off over time, and a store credit account lets customers buy now and pay the store later. Understanding the differences helps consumers manage spending and avoid debt. Because debit cards use money the buyer already has, they can help people avoid debt, but they offer fewer fraud protections than some credit cards.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain forms of financial exchange (cash, credit, debit, electronic funds transfer, etc.)

questions.question: Felipe notices that customers often ask the same three questions about the store's return policy. He creates a one-page handout and asks his manager if the store can use it. Felipe is showing
questions.explanation: Initiative. Felipe noticed a problem and took action to solve it, then followed proper channels by asking his manager. This shows initiative. Dependence means relying on others to act, indecision means having trouble making choices, and stubbornness means refusing to change. Initiative like this can improve customer service and get noticed by managers. Asking the manager first was important, because initiative works best when it follows company procedures. Employees who notice problems customers face are often the source of practical improvements.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the importance of demonstrating initiative

questions.question: Which of the following is a common advantage of a career as an entrepreneur?

options.A: Fewer working hours in the first year

questions.explanation: Being your own boss. Entrepreneurs make their own decisions and can build businesses around their interests and values. However, their income isn't guaranteed, they take on financial risk, and many work long hours, especially at first. Understanding both the rewards and challenges helps people decide whether entrepreneurship is right for them. Entrepreneurs also have the chance to earn more than they might as employees if the business succeeds. Many entrepreneurs say the independence and sense of ownership are worth the risk.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a natural resource used in production?
questions.explanation: Timber. Natural resources, also called land, are materials that come from nature, such as timber, water, minerals, and oil. A worker's skills are labor, a delivery truck is a capital good, and a business owner's idea and willingness to take risks represent entrepreneurship. Businesses combine these resources to produce goods and services. Every business uses some combination of these four factors of production. Because resources are limited, businesses must decide how to use them efficiently.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of economic resources

questions.question: Leaders inspire others mainly by
questions.explanation: Sharing a vision by example. Inspiring leaders communicate a clear, meaningful vision, show enthusiasm, and model the behavior they expect, which motivates others to give their best. Threats may force short-term compliance but reduce commitment, secrecy makes people feel excluded, and taking credit for every success discourages others. Inspiration builds long-term engagement. For example, a leader who works alongside the team during a busy period shows commitment that encourages others to do the same. People are more likely to follow leaders whose actions match their words. Inspiration also comes from showing people how their work connects to something meaningful.

questions.question: Purchasing helps a business by

options.A: getting what it needs at good value.

questions.explanation: Getting what it needs at good value. Purchasing involves finding suppliers, comparing prices and quality, negotiating terms, and ordering what the business needs to operate. Good purchasing helps control costs and keeps operations running smoothly. Selling to customers is part of sales, creating ads is promotion, and hiring is a human resources activity. Purchasing agents also build relationships with suppliers and make sure items arrive on time and meet quality standards. Good purchasing decisions can lower costs significantly, which directly improves profit.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of purchasing

questions.question: The accounting equation is
questions.explanation: Assets = liabilities + owner's equity. The accounting equation shows that everything a business owns, its assets, is financed either by borrowing, its liabilities, or by the owners, its equity. The balance sheet is organized around this equation. The other formulas aren't real accounting equations. Every transaction a business records keeps the equation in balance. For example, if a business has $50,000 in assets and owes $20,000, the owner's equity is $30,000. This equation is the foundation of double-entry accounting.

questions.question: Why is ongoing education important for workers?

options.A: It guarantees a promotion every year
options.C: Job skills and technology keep changing
options.D: Education is only needed before a first job

questions.explanation: Job skills and technology keep changing. Technology, laws, and business practices change constantly, so workers need to keep learning to stay effective and competitive. Ongoing education can include classes, certifications, workshops, and online courses. Employers regularly update equipment and methods, learning continues throughout a career, and education improves chances of advancement but doesn't guarantee promotions. Many employers support ongoing education by paying for training or offering tuition assistance, because skilled workers help the business stay competitive. Workers who keep learning are also better prepared if they need to change jobs or careers.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the need for ongoing education as a worker

questions.question: Positive customer relations help a business by

options.B: reducing the number of loyal customers.

questions.explanation: Encouraging repeat business and referrals. When customers feel valued and well served, they are more likely to return and recommend the business to others, which lowers the cost of finding new customers. Positive relations reduce complaints rather than increasing them, can't replace good products, and build loyalty rather than reducing it. Positive relations also help businesses recover from mistakes, because loyal customers are more forgiving when problems occur. Satisfied customers often share their experiences online and with friends, bringing in new customers at little cost.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of positive customer relations

questions.question: A company that pays employees by depositing their wages directly into their bank accounts is using
questions.explanation: Electronic funds transfer. Electronic funds transfer (EFT) moves money electronically from one account to another, as with direct deposit, online bill payments, and wire transfers. Barter exchanges goods or services without money, cash on delivery means paying when a product arrives, and a money order is a prepaid paper payment. Direct deposit is fast, secure, and convenient for both employers and employees. EFT also reduces the cost and risk of handling paper checks.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain forms of financial exchange (cash, credit, debit, electronic funds transfer, etc.)

questions.question: A manager at Fresh Fields Market wants to recognize an employee who shows initiative. Which employee's behavior best fits?

options.A: Waiting for a manager to assign every task
options.C: Ignoring a spill because it isn't your job
options.D: Leaving work early when it's slow

questions.explanation: Restocking shelves without being asked. Initiative means seeing what needs to be done and doing it without being told. Restocking shelves during a slow period helps the business and shows a strong work ethic. Waiting for instructions, leaving early, and ignoring problems show a lack of initiative. Employers often reward initiative with more responsibility. Employees who show initiative often learn new skills and are considered first for promotions. Initiative should still fit within company policies, so employees should check with a manager before making major changes.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the importance of demonstrating initiative

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the Internet of Things (IoT)?

options.C: A smart thermostat controlled by an app
options.D: A paper calendar on the wall

questions.explanation: A smart thermostat controlled by an app. The Internet of Things refers to everyday devices, such as thermostats, refrigerators, watches, and factory sensors, that connect to the Internet and share data. A smart thermostat can be controlled remotely and can report energy use. Printed newspapers, handwritten lists, and paper calendars aren't connected to any network. IoT devices give businesses new ways to collect data and offer services. Businesses use IoT devices to track shipments, monitor equipment, and learn how customers use products.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the scope of the Internet

questions.question: A new team leader wants everyone to support her plan to cut project delivery times in half. Which approach will best enlist their support?

options.A: Tell people to follow without questions

questions.explanation: Explain how it benefits everyone. People are more likely to commit to a vision when they understand why it matters and how it benefits them and the organization. Demanding obedience without explanation reduces commitment, keeping the vision secret leaves people without direction, and constantly changing it causes confusion. Involving people in shaping the vision can also build support. When people see how the vision connects to their own goals, they are more likely to commit their time and energy.

performanceIndicator.text: Enlist others in working toward a shared vision

questions.question: If an employee discovers a small fire in a trash can at work, the employee should first

options.A: alert others and follow the plan.
options.B: finish his or her current task.
options.C: ignore it and hope it goes out.
options.D: post a photo on social media.

questions.explanation: Alert others and follow the plan. Emergencies require quick action to protect people. Alerting others, activating the alarm if needed, and following the workplace emergency plan, which may include using a fire extinguisher only if trained and safe, are the right first steps. Ignoring the fire, posting on social media, or finishing a task wastes critical time and puts lives at risk. Employees should only try to put out a fire if it is small, they are trained, and they have a clear exit. Workplaces often hold drills so employees know the plan before an emergency happens.

questions.question: Andre gets a text alert that $300 was charged to his online bank account at a store he has never visited. What should he do?

options.A: Reply to the text with his password
options.C: Wait to see if it happens again
options.D: Delete the alert and ignore it

questions.explanation: Contact his bank right away. An unfamiliar charge could mean his account information was stolen. Contacting the bank quickly allows it to block the card, investigate, and possibly reverse the charge. Waiting could lead to more losses, replying with a password is unsafe because the message could be a scam, and ignoring the alert leaves the problem unresolved. Most banks limit a customer's losses from fraud when it is reported quickly, so acting fast matters.

questions.question: After a customer slips on a wet floor in a store and hurts her wrist, what should the employee do after making sure she gets help?

options.A: Ask the customer to sign a waiver
options.B: Tell coworkers it was her fault
options.C: Mop the floor and say nothing

questions.explanation: Complete an incident report. Businesses need accurate records of accidents and injuries for safety, insurance, and legal reasons. Completing an incident report documents what happened, when, and how, which helps prevent similar accidents. Cleaning the floor is important, but staying silent hides the incident. Asking for a waiver afterward is inappropriate, and blaming the customer is unprofessional. Incident reports also help the business identify hazards, such as floors that need better warning signs or mats, so it can prevent future injuries. Reports should describe facts, not opinions or blame.

questions.question: A manager tells Aisha to update the price tags in aisle 4, then help unload a delivery, and finally clean the break room before 5 p.m. After the manager leaves, Aisha isn't sure which task to do first. What should she have done?

options.D: Asked a customer what to do

questions.explanation: Repeated the directions back. Repeating directions back to the speaker confirms understanding and gives the manager a chance to clarify the order or priorities. Starting with the easiest task may not match the manager's wishes, ignoring directions is unacceptable, and customers don't know the manager's instructions. Taking quick notes while the manager talked would also have helped. Confirming the order is especially important when tasks have deadlines, such as finishing the break room before 5 p.m.

questions.question: During a group project, no one has volunteered to organize the work. Tia creates a schedule, divides tasks based on each person's strengths, and checks in with everyone weekly. Tia is demonstrating
questions.explanation: Leadership. Tia is taking initiative to guide the group, organizing the work, and supporting teammates, which are key leadership behaviors, even though she wasn't assigned a leadership role. Procrastination means delaying work, micromanagement means controlling every detail, and indecision means being unable to make choices. Weekly check-ins without excessive control support the team. Her actions show that leadership is about helping a group succeed, not just holding a title. Leaders like Tia often earn respect by helping others succeed rather than by giving orders.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good practice for managing online financial accounts:

options.B: Logging in on public Wi-Fi without protection
options.D: Using the same password for every account

questions.explanation: Monitoring account activity regularly. Checking online accounts regularly helps people spot unauthorized charges, errors, and low balances quickly. Using the same password everywhere, logging in on unsecured public Wi-Fi, and sharing login details increase the risk of fraud and identity theft. Many banks also offer alerts that notify users of large or unusual transactions. Strong, unique passwords and two-factor authentication add more protection. Many banks let customers set alerts for large purchases, low balances, or logins from new devices.

questions.question: Which of the following behaviors would most likely signal to a manager that a new employee has self-confidence:

options.B: Sharing an idea clearly in a meeting

questions.explanation: Sharing an idea clearly in a meeting. Self-confident employees trust their abilities and are willing to share ideas and take on challenges. Speaking clearly in a meeting shows confidence. Refusing new tasks, apologizing constantly, and avoiding eye contact can signal a lack of confidence. Confidence can be built through preparation, practice, and learning from mistakes. Self-confidence is different from arrogance: confident employees also listen to others and admit when they are wrong. Employers often look for confident employees for customer-facing roles because customers trust people who seem sure of their knowledge.

questions.question: Many retailers now use self-checkout machines. What is one impact of this technology on the business?
questions.explanation: Lower checkout labor costs. Self-checkout lets one employee oversee several registers, which can reduce labor costs and shorten lines during busy times. However, it may increase theft or frustrate some customers. Self-checkout doesn't eliminate inventory or require stores to close earlier, and it often reduces wait times. Businesses must weigh these savings against possible losses from theft and the needs of customers who prefer a cashier. Many stores keep both self-checkout and staffed lanes for this reason.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify ways that technology impacts business

questions.question: Four students wrote personal goals during a career-planning class. Which student's goal is written most effectively?

options.D: Save $600 for a laptop by June 1

questions.explanation: Save $600 for a laptop by June 1. Effective goals are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound, often called SMART goals. Saving $600 by June 1 states exactly how much, for what, and by when, so progress can be tracked. The other goals are vague and have no amount or deadline, which makes it harder to plan and stay motivated. Writing goals down and reviewing them regularly also makes people more likely to reach them. A clear goal also makes it easier to decide how much to save each week.

questions.question: Which of the following is a career opportunity in entrepreneurship:

options.A: Joining a large company's payroll department
options.C: Working as a salaried bank teller

questions.explanation: Starting a food truck business. Entrepreneurs start and run their own businesses, taking on the risks and rewards of ownership. Starting a food truck is an entrepreneurial venture. Bank tellers, government clerks, and payroll employees work for organizations owned by others and usually earn set wages or salaries. Entrepreneurship can also include buying a franchise or freelancing. Many entrepreneurs start small, such as selling products online or offering services in their neighborhood, before growing into larger businesses.

questions.question: Leadership is the ability to
questions.explanation: Guide others toward goals. Leaders guide and influence people to work together toward shared goals. Leadership can come from anyone, not just people with formal titles. Completing every task alone, avoiding responsibility, and only following instructions don't involve influencing or guiding others. Good leaders communicate clearly, motivate others, and take responsibility for results. Leadership skills can be developed through school activities, clubs, sports, and work. Many organizations look for leadership potential when hiring, even for entry-level positions.

questions.question: Two coworkers often gossip about others and try to turn people against a new manager. Which response is best for an employee who wants to handle office politics professionally?

options.A: Post about it on social media
options.C: Join in so they don't target you
options.D: Repeat the gossip to the manager

questions.explanation: Stay neutral and avoid gossip. Professional employees avoid gossip, focus on their work, and build positive relationships with everyone. Staying neutral protects their reputation and keeps them out of conflicts. Joining in spreads harmful behavior, repeating gossip can make situations worse, and posting online is unprofessional. If gossip becomes harassment, it should be reported through proper channels. Treating the new manager respectfully and judging him or her by actions rather than rumors is the professional approach.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of office politics

questions.question: A small bakery has only one oven. If the owner uses it to bake extra bread for a catering order, she can't use it to bake cakes for the store that day. The cakes she gives up are the

options.B: selling price of the extra bread.

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost of the decision. Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative given up when a choice is made. Because resources like the oven are limited, using it for bread means giving up the cakes. A fixed cost doesn't change with output, profit is what remains after costs, and price is what customers pay. Understanding opportunity cost helps businesses use scarce resources wisely. Every choice involves an opportunity cost, because using a resource for one purpose means it can't be used for another at the same time. Comparing the value of each option helps the owner choose wisely.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of economic resources

questions.question: During a product demonstration, a customer keeps nodding, smiling, and picking up the product to look more closely. What do these nonverbal cues most likely suggest?
questions.explanation: The customer is interested. Nodding, smiling, and examining the product closely usually show interest and engagement. A salesperson who notices these cues might move toward answering questions or closing the sale. Bored customers may look away or check phones, angry customers may frown or tense up, and customers who want to leave may step back or look toward the exit. Salespeople should still confirm interest by asking questions, since nonverbal cues can sometimes be misread.

questions.question: Rhea has worked as an administrative assistant for ten years. Her company is moving all records to new cloud software next year. What would best help her keep her job skills current?

options.A: Take a course on the new software
options.B: Refuse to use the new software
options.C: Wait until the software is installed to learn anything
options.D: Ask a coworker to do all of her cloud tasks

questions.explanation: Take a course on the new software. Taking a course before the change prepares Rhea to use the software confidently and shows her employer she is adaptable. Refusing the new system could put her job at risk, waiting leaves her unprepared, and relying on a coworker doesn't build her own skills. Workers who keep learning are more valuable as their workplaces change. Learning new tools also makes her more valuable if the company later needs someone to help train others.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the need for ongoing education as a worker

questions.question: Theo works at a bank where employees wear business attire Monday through Thursday and business casual on Fridays. On Friday, he is meeting an important new client. What should he wear?

options.A: A costume to make the client laugh
options.B: Gym clothes, because it's a casual Friday
options.D: Business attire for the client meeting

questions.explanation: Business attire for the client meeting. Even on a business-casual day, dressing more formally for an important client meeting shows respect and professionalism. Gym clothes, pajamas, and costumes are inappropriate for a bank and could hurt the client's impression of Theo and the business. Employees should consider their audience when choosing what to wear. A good rule is to dress at least as formally as the people you are meeting. Dressing appropriately shows the client that Theo takes the meeting seriously.

questions.question: Callie is always willing to adjust her work when plans change, such as covering a different task when a coworker is out. Which desirable trait is she showing?
questions.explanation: Adaptability. Adaptability is the ability to adjust to new situations and changing demands, which is valuable in fast-moving workplaces. Stubbornness is resisting change, shyness relates to discomfort in social situations, and carelessness means not paying attention to details. Adaptable employees help teams keep working when unexpected problems arise. Adaptability has become even more important as technology and customer needs change quickly. Interviewers often ask candidates to describe a time they adjusted to a change because employers value this trait so highly.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify desirable personality traits important to business

questions.question: Kendra suggests that her company offer online training to save travel costs. Her manager says online training might be less engaging. Which response best defends her idea objectively?

options.D: Complain to coworkers after the meeting

questions.explanation: Share data from similar programs. Providing evidence, such as completion rates or employee feedback from similar programs, addresses the manager's concern directly and objectively. Insisting the manager is wrong ignores a valid point, dropping the idea gives up without discussion, and complaining afterward is unprofessional. Objective defense also involves acknowledging valid concerns and suggesting solutions. She might also suggest a small pilot program to test online training before the company commits fully. Responding to concerns with evidence shows that she respects her manager's opinion while still standing behind her idea.

questions.question: The manager of an animal shelter wants volunteers to help raise $20,000 for a new kennel. Which approach is most likely to inspire them?

options.A: Tell volunteers they must raise $500 each or leave
options.B: Ask only the newest volunteers to help
options.C: Share stories of animals the kennel will help
options.D: Send a short email with no explanation

questions.explanation: Share stories of animals the kennel will help. Personal stories connect the goal to something volunteers care about, helping them see why their effort matters. Threats can drive people away, an unexplained email doesn't build enthusiasm, and asking only new volunteers misses the support of experienced ones. Inspiring others often means connecting a goal to shared values. She might also share a progress chart so volunteers can see how close they are to the goal. Connecting a goal to people's values often motivates them more than rewards or pressure.

questions.question: Before her first sales presentation, Nora feels nervous. Which action would best help her build self-confidence?

options.A: Read every word from her notes
options.B: Tell the audience she isn't prepared

questions.explanation: Practice it several times. Practice helps Nora become familiar with her material, which reduces nervousness and builds confidence. Canceling avoids the challenge, reading every word makes her seem less prepared and less engaging, and telling the audience she isn't ready undermines her credibility. Preparation is one of the most reliable ways to build confidence. She might also practice in front of a friend and ask for feedback, which can make the real presentation feel more familiar. Feeling some nervousness is normal and can even help her stay focused.

questions.question: Which of the following behaviors helps build trust in relationships:

options.B: Changing your story to avoid blame

questions.explanation: Keeping promises. Trust grows when people consistently do what they say they will do. Keeping promises, being honest, and admitting mistakes show that someone is reliable. Sharing secrets, changing stories to avoid blame, and taking credit for others' work damage trust and can be hard to repair. Trust is essential for teamwork and customer relationships. Trust also grows when people are honest about what they can and can't do, instead of making promises they can't keep. Once trust is broken, it often takes a long time and consistent behavior to rebuild it.

questions.question: An employee with an achievement orientation

options.A: sets goals and works hard to meet them.
options.D: waits for others to set every goal.

questions.explanation: Sets goals and works hard to meet them. Achievement orientation is the drive to set and meet high standards. People with this trait set goals, seek feedback, and look for ways to improve. Avoiding challenges, doing the minimum, and relying on others to set every goal show low motivation. Employers value achievement-oriented employees because they push for better results. Achievement-oriented employees often track their progress and look for ways to improve, even when they are already doing well. They also tend to bounce back from setbacks by learning from what went wrong.

questions.question: When evaluating online information for a business report, a writer should check whether the source

options.A: is current and comes from a credible author.
options.B: has the most colorful website design.
options.C: is the first result in a search.
options.D: agrees with what the writer already believes.

questions.explanation: Is current and comes from a credible author. Reliable sources are up to date, written by qualified people or organizations, and supported by evidence. Website design, search ranking, and agreement with the writer's opinions don't show whether information is accurate. In fact, relying only on sources that agree with you can lead to biased reports. Writers should also look for evidence, such as data or citations, and compare information across several reliable sources. Checking the date matters especially for topics that change quickly, such as technology and markets.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate quality and source of information

questions.question: Kenji is applying online for a summer job at a bank. Which of the following is the best advice for him?

options.B: Submit it without reading the job requirements
options.C: Use all capital letters for every answer

questions.explanation: Proofread before submitting. Proofreading helps catch spelling and grammar errors that could create a poor first impression. Copying another applicant's answers is dishonest, skipping the job requirements may mean applying for a poor fit, and using all capital letters is hard to read and looks unprofessional. Applicants should also tailor their answers to the job and keep a copy of what they submitted for interview preparation. Many employers use software to screen online applications, so complete, accurate answers help an application get noticed.

questions.question: Jamal recently learned that a coworker's identity was stolen. Which of the following habits would best help Jamal protect his own personal information?

options.A: Posting your birth date and address online
options.C: Carrying your Social Security card everywhere
options.D: Using the same password on all accounts

questions.explanation: Shredding documents with personal information. Identity thieves look for personal information, such as account numbers and Social Security numbers, in trash, online profiles, and stolen wallets. Shredding documents keeps that information out of the wrong hands. Posting personal details, carrying a Social Security card unnecessarily, and reusing passwords make it easier for thieves to steal identities. Other protections include checking credit reports regularly and using strong, unique passwords. People should also be careful about what they post online, since thieves can use details like birth dates to guess passwords or answer security questions.

questions.question: Marcus feels frustrated when a coworker criticizes his idea during a meeting. Instead of responding angrily, he takes a breath, asks the coworker to explain her concerns, and considers them. Marcus is demonstrating
questions.explanation: Emotional intelligence. Recognizing his frustration, controlling his reaction, and trying to understand the coworker's view are all parts of emotional intelligence. This helps keep the discussion productive and the relationship positive. Technical skill relates to specific job tasks, physical stamina relates to the body, and financial literacy relates to managing money. None of these describe how Marcus handled his emotions. Responding calmly also makes it more likely that the coworker will listen to Marcus's ideas in the future.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of emotional intelligence

questions.question: Owen, a new supervisor, wants his team to trust him. Last week he told an employee he would look into her schedule request, but he forgot. What should he do?

options.A: Admit the mistake and follow up now
options.C: Pretend he never made the promise
options.D: Ignore it and hope she forgets

questions.explanation: Admit the mistake and follow up now. Admitting a mistake and correcting it shows honesty and accountability, which can actually strengthen trust. Pretending the promise didn't happen or blaming software is dishonest, and ignoring the request suggests her needs don't matter. Leaders build trust through small, consistent actions over time. Owen could also keep a simple list of promises and requests so he doesn't forget them in the future. Employees tend to trust leaders who own their mistakes more than leaders who pretend to be perfect. Following up quickly also shows the employee that her request matters to him.

questions.question: A retailer's analytics team wants to mine five years of customer purchase data to find new sales opportunities. Which of the following should be its biggest ethical concern?
questions.explanation: Using data without permission. Data mining can reveal useful patterns, but using personal data in ways customers didn't agree to violates their privacy and trust. Businesses should be transparent about what they collect and how they use it. Finding trends, improving recommendations, and analyzing traffic patterns are common, legitimate uses of data when privacy is respected. Laws in many places now require businesses to explain what data they collect and to give customers some control over how it is used. Businesses that misuse data can lose customers' trust even when they haven't broken the law.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the importance of ethics in data mining

questions.question: When defending an idea objectively, a person should

options.A: raise his or her voice to win.

questions.explanation: Support it with evidence. Defending an idea objectively means using facts, data, and logical reasoning rather than emotion or personal attacks. This helps others evaluate the idea fairly. Raising your voice, criticizing others, and refusing to answer questions make people defensive and less likely to support the idea. Being open to questions also shows confidence in the idea. Listening carefully to objections and responding calmly also makes others more willing to consider the idea.

questions.question: Dmitri is writing a report on smartphone sales for his manager. He finds two sources. Source A is a 2019 blog post with no author that says sales are growing quickly. Source B is a report published this year by a market research firm that surveyed 5,000 consumers and explains its methods. Which source should he use?

options.A: Source B, because it is current and explains its methods
options.B: Source A, because blogs are always written by industry experts
options.C: Either source, because all online information is equal
options.D: Source A, because older data is more reliable

questions.explanation: Source B, because it is current and explains its methods. Source B is recent, comes from an identifiable research firm, and explains how its data was collected, which makes it more credible. Blogs aren't always accurate, especially without an author, older data may be outdated in a fast-changing market, and online sources vary greatly in quality. Evaluating sources carefully leads to better business decisions. He could also look for a second recent, credible source to confirm the findings. Reports that explain their methods let readers judge how much to trust the results.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate quality and source of information

questions.question: Gabriela, a new store manager, wants her staff to help make the store the top-rated location in the region for customer service. Which action would best enlist their support?

options.A: Post the goal on a sign and say nothing else
options.B: Threaten to cut hours if ratings don't improve
options.C: Ask staff for ideas to improve service
options.D: Tell staff the goal is only for managers

questions.explanation: Ask staff for ideas to improve service. Inviting employees to contribute ideas gives them ownership of the vision and makes them more committed to achieving it. A sign alone doesn't explain or involve anyone, threats create fear rather than commitment, and excluding employees from the goal makes no sense since they deliver the service. Employees who help shape a goal usually work harder to reach it. Gabriela can also share progress regularly and celebrate improvements to keep the team motivated.

performanceIndicator.text: Enlist others in working toward a shared vision
